Conclusions
Here we show that vitamin C and E supplementation may reduce fasting blood glucose and HbA1c levels in subjects metabolically
compromised. However, and similar to a previous meta-analysis on the effects of vitamin C (Mason et al., 2021) this reduction is
unlikely to have a clinically meaningful effect. In contrast, previous data reported that vitamin c supplementation shows a hypoten-
sive effect (Mason et al., 2021). Here, we show that this effect can be extrapolated to vitamin E and vitamin C þ E supplementation.
It should however be noted that we found a large heterogeneity among all the studies and most of the variables. Therefore, future
work should further investigate the source of this heterogeneity as antioxidant supplementation may not be save for all people in all
conditions.
